themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 41 THIS WEEK—a 507% increase from the 6.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting rapid pavement or surface degradation affecting multiple blocks in Crown Heights/Prospect Heights.
evidence: 41 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.79, the highest anomaly in dataset)
507% increase represents the most dramatic spike across all complaint categories
Concurrent spike in Street Sign - Dangling complaints (6 last week vs. 0.5 avg, +1100%), suggesting weather damage or structural failure
reporting_angles: Field verification: document potholes, cracked asphalt, or uneven surfaces on major commercial and residential corridors (Atlantic Ave, Nostrand Ave, Franklin Ave)
Interview DOT about inspection schedules and repair backlogs; cross-reference with DOB permit data showing 294 alteration filings (possible construction-related ground damage)

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 27 THIS WEEK—a 293% spike from the 6.9-complaint weekly baseline—signaling a potential influx of Uber/Lyft activity or parking/traffic violations in the district.
evidence: 27 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.14)
293% increase correlates with sustained high illegal parking complaints (2,050 over 90 days), suggesting vehicles are blocking or occupying parking illegally
No prior Reddit discussion or CB agenda item, suggesting this is an emerging operational problem rather than long-standing advocacy issue
reporting_angles: Interview TLC enforcement and NYPD traffic division about whether there has been a recent surge in ride-hailing driver violations (double-parking, blocking hydrants, illegal stops)
Survey residents and businesses on Atlantic Ave and Nostrand Ave about whether they've noticed increased for-hire vehicle congestion or aggressive driving

themes_detail.label: Animals in Parks Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-a-park complaints exploded to 6 THIS WEEK—an 860% increase from the 0.6-complaint weekly average—indicating a potential wildlife incursion or loose-animal problem in Prospect Park or neighborhood green spaces.
evidence: 6 animal-in-a-park complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.27)
860% spike is among the highest statistical anomalies in the dataset
Community board budget requests include 'Reconstruct or upgrade a building in a park,' suggesting known park infrastructure vulnerabilities that could enable animal access
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks about specific animal sightings this week (rats, raccoons, coyotes) and whether park barriers or maintenance issues have created entry points
Interview residents near Prospect Park and smaller green spaces (Marcus Garvey Park, St. John's Place green) about observations and safety concerns

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Spike
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 14 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 387% increase from the 2.9-complaint weekly average—suggesting widespread ventilation failures or building-system problems (possibly heat/HVAC-related) affecting multiple units.
evidence: 14 indoor air quality complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.66)
387% increase coincides with heat-wave or seasonal HVAC demand, but timing suggests building-level system failures
Convergence: 3,859 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days (the #1 complaint category) + 623 plumbing complaints + this spike suggests interconnected building-system breakdown
reporting_angles: Identify buildings with multiple complaints filed during the spike window; file FOIL requests for HPD/DOB inspection histories and violation records
Interview residents about mold, stale air, or HVAC non-functionality; cross-reference with heat/hot water complaint clusters to target buildings with systemic heating/ventilation failures

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints surged to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 700% increase from the 0.5-complaint weekly average—pointing to possible construction activity, storm damage, or deliberate tree removal in the district.
evidence: 4 illegal tree damage complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.95)
700% spike with 457 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (294 alterations, 84 new buildings, 13 demolitions) suggests construction-related tree damage
Convergence: Community board repeatedly budgets for 'Reconstruct or upgrade a building in a park' and 'park, building, or access improvements,' implying tree/canopy degradation is a chronic concern
reporting_angles: Cross-reference DOB permit locations with illegal tree damage complaint addresses to identify which construction projects may be responsible
Interview Parks Department about enforcement actions and whether there is a pattern of contractors or private actors removing or damaging street trees without permits
